title: introduce-auth-abstraction-layer-and-safe-upgrade-path-for-sso-jwt-libs
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary:
We need a low-risk, observable migration path to upgrade critical auth dependencies (JWT/OAuth libraries, SAML adapters and underlying crypto bindings) without impacting customer-facing authentication flows or introducing broad service restarts.

Goal:
1) Introduce a thin Auth Abstraction Layer (AAL) that decouples calling code from concrete third-party auth libs.
2) Implement runtime shims that allow side-by-side deployment of the old and new auth stacks and controlled traffic migration via feature flags and routing.
3) Execute upgrades for jwtverify, oauth-client, and saml-adapter libraries and swap crypto bindings to the vetted OpenSSL backport in a canary-first rollout.

Why this approach:
- Previous efforts replaced libs across services in-place and caused unexpected token parsing regressions and increased restarts.
- AAL + shims reduces blast radius, enables rollback by toggling routing, and provides improved telemetry for regression detection.

Technical plan (high level):
1) Audit call sites and create an interface spec for AAL (token parsing, validation, introspection, SSO assertion handling, error map). Record edge-cases and non-conforming behavior. Link: https://confluence.redwood/auth-aal-spec (placeholder).
2) Implement AAL in auth-common module; introduce v2 interfaces while keeping v1 adapters intact. Provide adapter shims that map old library error shapes to the AAL error map.
3) Add a feature-flag driven runtime router (FFK) in auth-proxy to choose adapter implementation per-token-source. Support per-customer and per-route scoping for Dedicated/Private customers.
4) Upgrade libraries in a separate branch: proposed targets jwtverify 3.x -> 4.1, oauth-client 2.9 -> 3.0, saml-adapter 1.5 -> 2.0 and OpenSSL backport 1.1.1 -> 1.1.1k-fips (build verified).
5) Implement dynamic loading where feasible to avoid 100% service restarts: plugin loader with symbol isolation for native bindings.
6) Add extensive unit tests, contract tests, and an intra-service fuzz harness for token parsing.
7) Canary rollout: 1% of internal traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
8) Provide migration runbook, rollback steps, and a postmortem checklist for any incidents.

Monitoring and telemetry:
- Add dedicated metrics: tokens_accepted_by_adapter, tokens_rejected_by_adapter, token_parse_latency, auth_error_class (mapped to AAL error map), and canary_failure_rate.
- Hook these metrics into existing Console dashboards and add a short-lived runbook dashboard for the rollout.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Introducing AAL increases initial surface area and developer friction until adapters are migrated. We accept this short-term cost to get safe long-term upgradeability.
- Dynamic native binding loading requires careful build and packaging; will increase CI complexity.

Rollout strategy and safety gates:
- Unit and contract tests: 100% pass required.
- Canary thresholds: token_parse_latency must not regress >15th percentile by >20% and error rate must be <0.5% above baseline for 30 minutes.
- Manual approval required at each ramp step from oncall + security eng.

Artifacts and PRs:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/auth-aal-spec (placeholder)
- Initial implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-common/pull/412 (WIP)
- Canary config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-configs/pull/87 (WIP)

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full replace of all customer-managed on-prem packages. We'll treat Private as a follow-up (because binary packaging and FIPS constraints add release complexity).

Acceptance criteria (see list field), and see comments for in-flight blockers and review feedback.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Priya: Initial scope and spec posted. Ran a quick audit across services and identified ~12 distinct token parsing call patterns; 3 of them rely on undocumented error codes.

2025-02-19 - Liam: Prototype AAL interface sketched (PR #401). Need alignment on whether AAL should return normalized HTTP error codes or internal enums — leaning towards enums to preserve mapping from legacy libs.

2025-02-25 - Security (A. Martinez): Requesting a formal artifact that lists any behavior changes for SAML assertion validation and a plan for signature verification fallbacks. Marked security_review_required=true.
2025-02-28 - Eng Tech Lead (R. Gupta): Prototype dynamic loader works in staging but uncovered a symbol collision when both bindings are resident. Added task to namespace native symbols during build.

2025-03-03 - CI: Contract tests failing intermittently for the legacy adapter shim on long-lived sessions. Investigating KV cache interaction as possible cause; next action: add deterministic session playback tests.
2025-03-03 - Liam: Rebased PR #412 to main and split the dynamic loader into separate package; opened follow-up ENG-60910 to harden native build artifacts.
2025-03-03 - Priya: Scheduled canary window and pager rotations. Oncall for first ramp will be @sre-team and @auth-eng. Added runbook draft to attachments.
acceptance_criteria: AAL implemented and merged into auth-common with backward-compatible adapter shims
All call sites compiled against AAL with no functional changes in baseline test suite
Upgraded libraries built and validated in staging with native binding namespaced to avoid collisions
Contract tests and fuzzing show no new parse/regression failures for identified token patterns
Canary rollout runbook, dashboards, and automatic rollback thresholds configured
Security review completed and signed off by Security team
Documentation updated (Confluence and runbook) and post-rollout verification checklist created
notes: Follow-up tickets expected: binary packaging for Private (ENG-60945), native build hardening (ENG-60910), and customer communication templates for Dedicated (ENG-60977).
Estimate may increase if we uncover additional legacy parsing edge cases during contract test expansion.
Coordination: schedule joint workspace with SRE, Security, and Platform Release to cover canary windows in multi-region deployments.
